01 / The recordA geometry of exchanges

Two strands
per exchange.

One comes from your message, the other from the model’s reply. Each has a numbered address in the record.

This study counts letters and digits in three groups. Rearranging the same characters gives the same fractions.

What is being counted? +

Letters A–Z (ignoring case) take values 1–26. Letters and digits 1–9 are grouped by their remainder after division by 3. The fractions count how much of your text falls in each group. This study skips spaces, punctuation, zero and other characters.

The fractions sum to 1. Their distance from the reference triple (0.302, 0.351, 0.347), supplied in Mindgut’s brief, sets how far the point sits from the helix’s axis. Your text changes address #1; the other 83 coordinates are examples.
